title: Maximize Min Plus Max of a Subarray
statement:
You are given an array `a` of `n` positive integers, with `n ≥ 2`.

Consider every subarray (contiguous block) of `a` that has **more than one element**. The value of a subarray is the **sum of its minimum element and its maximum element**.

Print the largest value over all such subarrays.

**Follow-up:** the interviewer expected you to reason about why a particular family of subarrays is enough, rather than examining all of them.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated positive integers `a[0] … a[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum value of (minimum + maximum) over all subarrays of length at least 2.

examples.explanation: The adjacent pair [1, 5] gives 1 + 5 = 6. Nothing beats it: [3, 1] gives 4, [1, 4] and [4, 1] give 5, and longer subarrays such as the whole array also have minimum 1 and maximum 5.
The only subarray with more than one element is the whole array: min 7 plus max 7.
The subarray [10, 1] gives 11. The whole array also gives 1 + 10 = 11, and [1, 9] gives only 10.

hints: Trying all subarrays costs O(n^2) or worse. Ask which subarrays could ever be the best one.
Take any subarray of length at least 2 and look at its maximum element. At least one of its neighbours inside the subarray exists.
That neighbour is at least as large as the subarray minimum, so the two-element subarray formed by the maximum and that neighbour is at least as good. Only adjacent pairs matter.

def gen(rng):
    def fmt(a):
        return str(len(a)) + '\n' + ' '.join(map(str, a))

    tests = [
        fmt([1, 1]),
        fmt([5, 5, 5]),
        fmt([10 ** 9, 10 ** 9]),
        fmt([1, 10 ** 9]),
        fmt([3, 1, 4, 1, 5]),
        fmt([10, 1, 1, 9]),
        fmt([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]),
        fmt([6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1]),
        fmt([9, 1, 9]),
        fmt([1, 9, 1, 9, 1]),
    ]
    for n in (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30):
        for hi in (3, 10, 1000):
            tests.append(fmt([rng.randint(1, hi) for _ in range(n)]))
    tests.append(fmt([rng.randint(1, 10 ** 9) for _ in range(3000)]))
    N = 100000
    tests.append(fmt([rng.randint(1, 10 ** 9) for _ in range(N)]))
    tests.append(fmt([rng.randint(1, 5) for _ in range(N)]))
    tests.append(fmt([10 ** 9 - (i % 1000) for i in range(N)]))
    tests.append(fmt(sorted(rng.randint(1, 10 ** 9) for _ in range(N))))
    return tests
